root.claim: A single deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Provide two fast tape procedures, place them inside the Gaussian-resampling and synthetic-transform reduction of the integer product to a convolution, then check precision and exact recovery and add up the costs of all phases.

motivation.text: Scanning $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so savings are needed in both address movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving is a fixed power of the logarithm, $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$, rather than a $\log\log$ factor, even though $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small.
